title: Burning and Suppression of Solids
objective: Examine burning and extinction characteristics of diverse solid fuel geometries in microgravity under forced air flow inside the Microgravity Science Glovebox.
fuel: Solid: PMMA rods, flat sheets, acrylic spheres, cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) fabrics, and Nomex samples
hardware: MSG with SPICE flow duct

conditions.ambient: ISS MSG cabin air with nitrogen dilution in SPICE flow duct

variables: Opposed and concurrent forced flow velocity
Extinction flow threshold and nitrogen suppression
sensors: High-resolution still camera with radiometric lens
earthApplications: Spacecraft and terrestrial fire-resistant material screening standards
Ventilation-controlled fire suppression strategies in enclosed cabins

title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
objective: Investigate solid-fuel flammability limits, flame spread rates, and radiative/low-flow quenching in microgravity as a function of oxygen concentration and forced ventilation velocity.
fuel: Solid: Acrylic (PMMA) slabs and rods, cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) fabrics, and Nomex textiles
hardware: MSG with SPICE flow duct

conditions.ambient: ISS MSG with SPICE flow duct and controlled O2/N2 flow

earthApplications: Improvement of NASA-STD-6001 material flammability testing
Firefighter thermal protective textile char and heat-flux modeling

title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment - I
objective: Measure large-scale concurrent flame spread and cabin oxygen consumption over a 0.4 m x 1.0 m cotton-fiberglass sample inside an uncrewed Cygnus cargo spacecraft after ISS departure.
fuel: Solid: SIBAL fabric sheet (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass), 0.4 m wide x 1.0 m long
hardware: Saffire flow duct inside Cygnus OA-6 spacecraft

conditions.ambient: Cygnus OA-6 pressurized cargo cabin air

variables: Flame length and pyrolysis zone thickness
Cabin pressure rise and O2/CO2 concentration change
sensors: Oxygen and carbon dioxide gas sensors
earthApplications: Large-scale enclosure fire modeling for mines, tunnels, and submarines

title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment - II
objective: Determine microgravity flammability limits and flame spread across nine 5 cm x 30 cm spacecraft material samples (including PMMA of varying thickness, Nomex, silicone, and SIBAL) inside Cygnus OA-7.
fuel: Solid: Nine 5 cm x 30 cm strips (cotton-fiberglass, Nomex, silicone, and flat/grooved PMMA slabs)
hardware: Saffire flow duct inside Cygnus OA-7 spacecraft

conditions.ambient: Cygnus OA-7 pressurized cargo cabin air

variables: Concurrent and opposed flame spread rate

title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment - III
objective: Characterize large-scale concurrent flame spread rate and steady burning limits over a 0.4 m x 1.0 m cotton-fiberglass panel at two forced ventilation flow speeds inside Cygnus OA-5.
fuel: Solid: SIBAL composite fabric sheet (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass), 0.4 m wide x 1.0 m long

variables: Axial forced flow velocity (0.20 and 0.30 m/s)

title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment
objective: Measure particle size distributions and morphology of smoke aerosols generated by overheated spacecraft materials in microgravity to improve spacecraft smoke detector design and calibration.
fuel: Solid/liquid pyrolysis: Kapton wire insulation, Teflon, silicone rubber, cellulose paper, and lamp oil
hardware: MSG (Microgravity Science Glovebox)

conditions.ambient: ISS MSG cabin air in enclosed aging duct

variables: Smoke particle diameter distribution moments (count, surface, mass)
sensors: Thermal precipitator TEM electron microscopy samplers

title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight
objective: Re-examine microgravity smoke particle size distributions from spacecraft materials over extended pyrolysis temperatures and aging durations to refine next-generation exploration smoke detectors.

title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
objective: Study spherical liquid-droplet combustion and evaluate the effectiveness of gaseous fire suppressants by diluting the atmosphere with carbon dioxide (CO2) and helium (He) in microgravity.
fuel: Liquid droplet: Methanol and n-heptane isolated droplets (~2 to 5 mm initial diameter)
hardware: CIR/MDCA (Combustion Integrated Rack / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus)

conditions.ambient: CIR chamber with O2/N2 diluted with CO2 and helium (He) suppressants

variables: CO2 and helium inert diluent mole fraction
Radiative vs diffusive extinction droplet diameter
sensors: Chamber pressure and gas composition transducers
earthApplications: Clean-agent inert gas and CO2 fire suppression system optimization
Ultra-fine water mist fire suppression kinetics for data centers and marine vessels

title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2
objective: Investigate spherical droplet burning rates, soot shell dynamics, radiative extinction, and second-stage low-temperature cool-flame transitions of pure and bi-component alkane droplets in microgravity.
fuel: Liquid droplet: n-heptane, n-octane, n-decane, methanol, and bi-component droplet mixtures (1.5 to 4.0 mm spherical droplets)
hardware: CIR/MDCA (Combustion Integrated Rack / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus)

conditions.ambient: CIR/MDCA sealed chamber (15% to 30% O2, 0.5 to 3.0 atm)

sensors: UV/visible intensified array cameras (OH* and CH* radicals)
earthApplications: Clean, high-efficiency liquid fuel spray combustion in automotive and aviation engines
Chemical kinetic validation for low-temperature alkane oxidation

title: Cool Flames Investigation
objective: Observe quasi-steady low-temperature cool flames of heavy liquid alkane droplets in microgravity without hot-flame ignition to characterize low-temperature oxidation and extinction.
fuel: Liquid droplet: Heavy alkane droplets (n-dodecane, n-decane, n-heptane) in MDCA
hardware: CIR/MDCA (Combustion Integrated Rack / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus)

conditions.ambient: CIR/MDCA chamber at controlled O2 and pressure

variables: Vapor cloud condensation and extinction diameter
earthApplications: Homogeneous charge compression ignition (HCCI) and low-temperature engine design
Prevention of cool-flame auto-ignition hazards in fuel storage

title: ACME: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
objective: Investigate non-premixed spherical gaseous cool flames in microgravity, testing oxygen concentrations up to 85% O2 supplied from the porous spherical burner to map extreme high-O2 cool-flame and hot-flame boundaries.

hardware: CIR/ACME (Combustion Integrated Rack / Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments)

conditions.ambient: CIR/ACME chamber (highest O2 in PSI: up to 85% O2 injected from burner)

variables: Fuel dilution and mass flow rate
Cool-flame stability limits and radiative extinction

title: ACME: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames

variables: Applied electric field voltage and polarity
Ion current density (body-force proxy for partial gravity)

Active electrostatic flame stabilization and suppression
